# Introduction

`ndopred` applies the **IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria v3.1** (IUCN 2012)
using the interpretation given in the **Guidelines for Using the IUCN Red List
Categories and Criteria v16** (IUCN Standards and Petitions Committee, March
2024). Both documents are in `methodology/`. Section numbers cited below refer
to the Guidelines unless stated otherwise.

The case study is a **national (Czech) Red List** built from NDOP occurrence
records. Two documents that a national list also needs are **not** bundled here
and are not implemented:

* *Guidelines for Application of IUCN Red List Criteria at Regional and National
  Levels: Version 4.0* (IUCN 2012). This is where **RE** is defined, and where
  the downgrading/upgrading step for immigration from outside the region is
  specified. `ndopred` performs **no regional adjustment**: it produces a
  global-style category from Czech data only. That step remains manual.
* *Documentation Standards and Consistency Checks*.

# 1. What is automated, and what is not

Occurrence records support some criteria and not others. `ndopred` never infers
a judgement it has no data for; those are function arguments instead.

| Element | Source |
|---|---|
| EOO, AOO, number of locations, spatial trends | Computed from NDOP |
| Mature individuals, decline rate, fluctuations | Computed from NDOP counts, as **minimum observed values** |
| B(a) severe fragmentation (§4.8) | `severely_fragmented` — assessor |
| B(b)(iii) habitat decline (§4.6) | `habitat_decline` — assessor; NDOP carries no habitat data |
| D2 plausible threat (§8) | `d2_threat` — assessor |
| Criterion E | Not automated |

# 2. Spatial metrics

**AOO** is the count of occupied cells times the cell area (§4.10.2, eq. 4.1) on
the reference **2 × 2 km** grid (§4.10.3). Because AOO depends on where the grid
starts, `calculate_aoo()` tests a 4 × 4 lattice of grid origins and keeps the
**minimum** count, as §4.10.2 requires. A different grid size emits a warning:
estimates at other scales are not comparable with the criterion thresholds.

**EOO** is a minimum convex polygon (§4.9). Discontinuities and disjunctions are
deliberately *not* excluded — §4.9 strongly discourages that for criterion B1.
Where a hull cannot be built (fewer than three points, or a degenerate hull),
EOO is returned as `NA` and `reconcile_eoo_aoo()` substitutes AOO, per the rule
that EOO is never smaller than AOO.

**Locations** (§4.11) are a *threat-based* concept: "a geographically or
ecologically distinct area in which a single threatening event can rapidly
affect all individuals of the taxon present". That cannot be derived from
records. `calculate_locations()` returns a **distance-cluster surrogate**
(default 5 km) as a starting point for review, nothing more. Note also that
"in the absence of any plausible threat for the taxon, the term 'location'
cannot be used and the subcriteria that refer to the number of locations will
not be met" — a judgement only the assessor can make.

# 3. Time windows

Two different windows are used, because the criteria ask different questions.

* **Criterion B** describes the **current** distribution: §4.9 states that EOO
  and AOO "should not include areas where the species no longer exists". EOO,
  AOO and locations therefore use a short recent window (default 10 years).
* **Criterion A** measures reduction over **10 years or three generations,
  whichever is longer**, capped at 100 years (§4.4, §5.2).

Trends compare the recent window against the **immediately preceding window of
equal length**. Both windows use a **single shared grid origin**: minimising the
origin separately per period would compare two different grids and manufacture
change that is not there.

# 4. Criterion A

Thresholds are 90/70/50 % for A1 and 80/50/30 % for A2–A4. Basis (b) is used
when the reduction comes from counts ("an index of abundance appropriate to the
taxon") and basis (c) when it comes from a decline in AOO or EOO.

Reduction from counts is estimated with the **exponential** model of §4.5.1
(constant proportional rate), fitted as `log(N) ~ year` and projected over the
assessment window, floored at −100 %.

# 5. Criterion B

The area threshold must be met **and at least two of the three conditions**
(a) severe fragmentation or few locations, (b) continuing decline, (c) extreme
fluctuations. Subindices under (b) reflect only what was actually measured:
(i) from an EOO trend, (ii) from an AOO trend, (iv) from a trend in the number
of locations, (v) from a trend in mature individuals. **(iii) is never inferred.**

Because a trend resampled from opportunistic records carries noise — and §4.9
warns that convex-hull EOO is "less suitable as a method for comparing two or
more temporal estimates … for assessing reductions or continuing declines" — a
change smaller than `decline_tolerance` (default 5 %) is not asserted as a
continuing decline. Set it to 0 for the literal "decline at any rate" reading.

# 6. Criteria C and D

C1 thresholds are 25 % in 3 years or 1 generation (CR), 20 % in 5 years or 2
generations (EN), and 10 % in 10 years or 3 generations (VU) — whichever is
longer in each case. The observed rate is re-projected onto each category's own
reference period before comparison; a single 10-year rate must not be tested
against all three.

C2 requires a continuing decline **in numbers of mature individuals**; a purely
spatial trend does not satisfy it. C2a(i) caps the largest subpopulation at
50/250/1000, and C2a(ii) requires 90 %/95 %/100 % of mature individuals in one
subpopulation — the proportions differ by category.

## One switch for all abundance evidence

`evaluate_pop` decides whether the NDOP counts are fit to be used **at all**.
It gates criteria C and D1, criterion A basis (b), B(b)(v) and B(c)(iv)
together. The reason they move as a group is that they all rest on the same
records: a *trend* computed from thin or unrepresentative counts is no more
trustworthy than a *total* computed from them, and is in fact more exposed to
recording effort (§4.10.8). Letting the trend through while refusing the total
would drive criterion A from data the assessment has just declared unusable.

With the switch off, criterion A rests on the spatial trend alone — basis (c),
"a decline in area of occupancy, extent of occurrence and/or quality of
habitat". The single-species app sets it automatically for vertebrates and
plants whose counted records substantially cover a mature life stage, shows
the coverage figures and the skipped life stages, and lets the assessor
override the decision either way.

D1 applies at fewer than 50/250/1000 mature individuals.

**D2 is not applied from the numbers alone.** §8 is explicit: "simply meeting
the suggested (or any other) threshold for AOO or number of locations is not
sufficient", and literal application "results in massive over-listing". A
restricted taxon is reported as a **D2 candidate**; VU D2 follows only once the
assessor confirms a plausible threat capable of causing CR or EX in a very short
time.

# 7. Extreme fluctuations

§4.7 requires variation greater than one order of magnitude **and** a recurring
pattern of increases and decreases; §4.6 adds that "an observed decline should
not be considered as a fluctuation unless there is evidence for this".
`calculate_pop_metrics()` therefore reports the max/min ratio, a count of
direction reversals, and a boolean `extreme_fluctuation` requiring a ratio ≥ 10,
at least two reversals, and at least five years of data. A steep monotonic
crash is a reduction, not a fluctuation.

# 8. Near Threatened

NT is defined by **proximity to Vulnerable**, not by its own criteria (§10.1),
so NT results are reported as "nearly meets …" rather than with a criteria code.
It is applied when:

* a reduction of 20–29 % is measured (§10.1 gives 20–25 % as a worked example);
* the criterion B area threshold is met together with exactly **one** of the
  three conditions;
* the population is below roughly twice the D1 threshold (§10.1 gives ~1,500
  mature individuals as NT and "more than 2,000" as not NT).

A restricted but stable and unthreatened taxon meeting **none** of the three B
conditions is **not** NT — §10.1 lists that case explicitly among those that
should not be listed.

# 9. DD and RE screens

**DD** (§10.3) is applied when fewer than three usable records exist, or when
AOO cannot be estimated, or when the taxon is absent from the recent window
without meeting the RE screen. §10.3 discourages liberal use of DD, so these are
deliberately narrow.

**RE** is a *screen*, not a determination. Neither bundled document defines a
years-since-last-record rule; RE belongs to the Regional Guidelines v4.0, and
§11.1 requires exhaustive surveys before any extinction listing, warning against
the "Romeo Error". `re_threshold_years` (default 50) therefore flags taxa for
survey follow-up and is a parameter, not a constant.

# 10. Known limitations

* NDOP is an opportunistic database. AOO, EOO and location counts are sensitive
  to recording effort (§4.10.8), and counts are minimum observed values, not
  population estimates (§4.3). Both bound the true values from below.
* Subpopulations (§4.2) are approximated by NDOP localities.
* No regional adjustment for immigration is applied (see the Introduction).
* Criterion E is not implemented.
